title: Lena and the Kitchen
premise: Coral Lockridge built her wedding-planning empire on the belief that love is a performance she can stage but never star in. When her estranged family's reunion threatens to expose the cracks in her polished life, she hires Theo Marchetti, a widowed baker facing the loss of his lease, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date turns devastatingly real, and as Coral helps Theo fight the predatory developer seizing his building, she discovers the developer is tied to the inheritance that once saved her own family — money bought with someone else's ruin. Forced to choose between protecting her career and doing justice outside the law, Coral exposes the truth at a high-profile wedding, sacrificing her reputation to save Theo's bakery, and finally lets herself be loved.
about_author: Z. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former catering manager who spent a decade watching love bloom over dessert tables before writing it down. They live near the coast with a sourdough starter named after their grandmother.

chapters.title: The Heart Is a Muscle
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At a flawless society wedding, Coral orchestrates another couple's happily-ever-after while deflecting her sister's summons to the Lockridge family reunion, where her mother expects a serious partner in attendance. Panicked, she impulsively asks Theo, the baker whose lemon tarts she's ordered for years, to play her boyfriend. Beat: control masking loneliness.

chapters.title: One Weekend, No Refunds
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo agrees to the arrangement because Coral's fee could cover a month of his failing bakery's rent, though he quietly dreads pretending again after losing his wife. They rehearse their backstory over flour and late-night coffee, and their invented history keeps sounding like something he wants. Beat: reluctant hope taking root.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the seaside Lockridge house, Coral performs the perfect couple while old wounds reopen: her mother's cold arithmetic about love, her sister Priya's suspicion, and a framed photo of the grandfather whose inheritance rescued them all. By dessert, Theo defends her against a cruel uncle with such sincerity the lie stops feeling like one. Beat: the fake becomes real.

chapters.title: What the Will Buried
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Sorting her grandfather's papers for the reunion, Priya finds an old deed suggesting the Lockridge fortune traces to a property taken from a business partner decades ago — a bakery, once called Marchetti & Sons. She says nothing, torn between loyalty and dread. Beat: inheritance revealed as theft.

chapters.title: Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Back home, Theo receives the developer's final offer: sell the bakery or face eviction in sixty days. Coral, visiting under a flimsy pretext, sees the eviction notice and recognizes the developer's parent company — Lockridge Holdings. She hides what she knows. Beat: guilt curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: Trainable, Containable
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral throws herself into work, staging a lavish engagement party while secretly digging into Lockridge Holdings' acquisition records. Theo shows up unannounced with bread and an unmistakable confession; she kisses him, then pulls away, terrified that loving him means losing everything she built. Beat: desire versus self-protection.

chapters.title: Priya's Evidence
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Coral with the deed and letters proving their grandfather cheated his partner — Theo's grandfather — out of the bakery that seeded the family fortune. She urges Coral to come forward; Coral refuses, arguing exposure will destroy them all. The sisters fracture. Beat: complicity made undeniable.

chapters.title: The Best-Laid Wedding
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Eviction day looms as Theo prepares to surrender the keys. He learns Coral has been quietly paying his suppliers and delaying the demolition permit through legal loopholes — small justices outside the law — but it isn't enough. Meanwhile Coral is booked to run the biggest wedding of her career, hosted by Lockridge Holdings itself. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Toast
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the climax wedding, with investors and her mother in the room, Coral abandons her script during the toast and tells the room the truth: the company's founding fortune was stolen from a baker, and the pattern continues today. She presents the deed, resigns mid-sentence, and walks out into Theo's waiting arms as her career detonates behind her. Beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: Lena and the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later, the bakery survives — renamed Lena's, after Theo's late wife, whose recipe book Coral helped restore — sustained by new community ownership and Priya's pro bono legal fight. Coral plans weddings again, but only ones she believes in, and her mother, chastened, finally visits. On a quiet morning, Theo proposes not with a ring but with a key. Beat: found family, earned love, home.
